full_text: He won the world Scrabble championship in French. He doesn't speak French. His name is Nigel Richards, a quiet New Zealander. His mother taught him Scrabble at twenty-eight, reportedly telling him he'd be no good at it because he couldn't spell. He became English world champion five times. He once cycled fourteen hours to a tournament, and cycled home afterward. Then he memorized the French dictionary, four hundred thousand words, in nine weeks, won the title, and thanked the audience through a translator. In 2024, at fifty-seven, he entered the Spanish world championship. A third language he doesn't speak. He won twenty-three of twenty-four games, with the first perfect scores ever recorded at the event, which makes him world champion in three languages, and a speaker of exactly one. He has never explained how. He turns down interviews with a smile, and walks away.
